title: Orientation layer — collapse repeated exact transforms
objective: Replace per-action transform layers with one orientation layer holding the composed exact state, updated in place while it is the last layer of the stack, so any number of rotations and reflections leave one layer.
context_summary: Accepted by the owner on 2026-09-20 for immediate implementation. Effect lightwell.geometry.orientation, payload {mirror, turns}, mirror first then clockwise quarter-turns. The four actions keep their durable history identities, controls and API. Plan updates the last layer when it is an orientation layer, else commits a new one. The old transform effect is removed and stacks holding it are refused explicitly. Coordinated with the content-space edits work, which places pixel layers before geometry layers; run after it lands so the host placement rule and this plan share one tree.

tasks.description: Implement the orientation layer in the core: payload, composition, planning rule, exact compile, and every fixture and journey that built transform layers.
extra_context: Replace Layer::transform and the TRANSFORM_EFFECT constant with an orientation payload and constructor; keep the Transform enum as the action vocabulary. Composition table and geometry are in the design.

Renderer, editor, registry, command contract, acceptance and performance code build transform layers today; move them to the orientation constructor and keep every existing identity, ordering, interleaving and EXIF proof passing with the new representation.
Do not add layer removal. Reaching neutral leaves a neutral layer.

acceptance_criteria: Four Rotate right actions leave one neutral orientation layer, four entries and a byte-identical render; undo steps back through the intermediate orientations.
Every sequence of up to three actions renders byte-identically to the stepwise reference on synthetic and EXIF-mirrored fixtures.
A transform after a crop appends; a further transform updates that layer; the crop composition is carried as the crop spec describes.
Stacks holding the old transform effect are refused as an unavailable effect without being rewritten.
Performance checklist answered: composition is integer arithmetic; no new allocation in planning or rendering.

expected_results: All proofs pass with the new representation.
